title: E: image formats and very wide figures
text:
NoteAbout this page



This page tests the panzoom extension with the knitr graphics devices and figure shapes used in practice: very wide collages (25 × 2 inches), and webp, svg and pdf output. Every figure is marked with #| panzoom: true and should open the pan/zoom viewer, except where a case says otherwise.
Cases with an expected opening view say so in their heading’s expect-fit attribute (contain, height or width), which the browser test checks. By default (fit: auto) very wide figures open at screen height from the left end, very tall ones at screen width from the top, and everything else whole.
Cases with a shift-scroll attribute say which way Shift+scroll should move the image: x (sideways), y (up and down) or none (it fits, so it stays put); zoomed-x means sideways after zooming in until the image extends past the screen both ways.
Cases with expect-scale="1" are smaller than the screen and must open at their real size (1 image pixel per screen pixel), not enlarged, and still zoom in.
webp comes from ragg’s agg_webp device: knitr has no built-in webp device, and agg_webp needs units = "in" because knitr passes sizes in inches.

11. Tall strip (4 × 15 in)

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height: 15

set.seed(2)
par(mfrow = c(8, 1), mar = c(2, 3, 2, 1))
```

title: E: image formats and very wide figures
text:
13. Large poster (24 × 18 in)
Opens whole; zoomed in, it extends past the screen both ways, and Shift+scroll moves sideways.

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-width: 24
#| fig-height: 18
#| fig-cap: "A 24 × 18 inch poster of 48 panels."

set.seed(3)
par(mfrow = c(6, 8), mar = c(2, 2, 2, 1))
for (i in 1:48) plot(cumsum(rnorm(100)), type = "l", main = paste("Panel", i), xlab = "", ylab = "")
```




A 24 × 18 inch poster of 48 panels.

title: E: image formats and very wide figures
text:
14. Gallery of two tall strips
Each strip opens at screen width and extends downwards: Left/Right do nothing (there is nowhere to go sideways) rather than switch strips; PageDown, PageUp and the buttons switch.

```{r}
#| panzoom:
#|   group: strips
#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height: 15
#| fig-cap:
#|   - "First strip."
#|   - "Second strip."

for (k in 1:2) {
  set.seed(10 + k)
  par(mfrow = c(8, 1), mar = c(2, 3, 2, 1))
  for (i in 1:8) plot(cumsum(rnorm(100)), type = "l", main = paste("Strip", k, "row", i), xlab = "", ylab = "")
}
```




First strip.







Second strip.

title: E: image formats and very wide figures
text:
15. png + cairo_pdf (dev: [png, cairo_pdf])
Like case 6, with the cairo PDF device, which embeds fonts and handles Unicode (µ, Greek letters) and transparency better than pdf. The page shows the png either way; a PDF figure only ever appears as the browser’s PDF viewer (case 7), whichever device wrote it.

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| dev: !expr c("png", "cairo_pdf")
#| fig-cap: "png shown, cairo_pdf written alongside (mu = 5, alpha = 0.05)."

filled.contour(volcano, color.palette = terrain.colors,
               plot.title = title(main = "mu = 5, alpha = 0.05"))
```




png shown, cairo_pdf written alongside (mu = 5, alpha = 0.05).

title: panzoom
text: This is a Quarto extension that opens figures in a full-screen viewer, built on Panzoom: scroll to zoom toward the cursor, drag to pan, double-click or 0 to reset, Esc to close. It attempts to match, and extend, the feature set of Quarto’s built-in lightbox. Source and documentation: https://github.com/sekoclancy/panzoom.

title: panzoom
text:
Chunk output
Mark a code cell with #| panzoom: true. Click the figure to open it, scroll to zoom toward the cursor, drag to pan, double-click to reset, Esc to close.

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 4

image(volcano, col = hcl.colors(100, "Viridis"), asp = 1 / 3)
```

title: panzoom
text:
Cross-referenced figure
Labeled figures work too (Figure 1). Options under #| panzoom: override the document’s settings for one cell: this figure zooms to 10 instead of the page’s 6, and hides the hint.

```{r}
#| label: fig-volcano
#| fig-cap: "Maunga Whau volcano."
#| panzoom:
#|   max-zoom: 10
#|   hint: false

filled.contour(volcano, color.palette = terrain.colors)
```







Figure 1: Maunga Whau volcano.

title: panzoom
text:
Markdown image



A markdown image with the .panzoom class.

title: panzoom
text:
Captions and galleries
The viewer shows the figure’s caption. Plots with the same group form a gallery: use the ‹ › buttons, ←/→ or a swipe to step through them. Subfigures of one figure are a gallery automatically.
```{r}
#| panzoom:
#|   group: volcano-views
#| fig-cap:
#|   - "Volcano heights as an image."
#|   - "The same data as a perspective plot."
#| layout-ncol: 2

image(volcano, col = hcl.colors(100, "Viridis"))
persp(volcano, theta = 135, phi = 30, col = "green3", shade = 0.5, border = NA)
```






Volcano heights as an image.







The same data as a perspective plot.





```{r}
#| label: fig-volcano-sub
#| fig-cap: "Two views of Maunga Whau, as subfigures."
#| fig-subcap: ["Contours", "Filled contours"]
#| layout-ncol: 2
#| panzoom: true

contour(volcano)
image(volcano)
```











(a) Contours











(b) Filled contours







Figure 2: Two views of Maunga Whau, as subfigures.

title: panzoom
panzoom
text:
Test pages
The same 12 lightbox situations (galleries, subfigures, captions with math, images in links, margin images, …) rendered four ways:

A: Quarto lightbox reference: Quarto’s built-in lightbox alone.
B: marked images + lightbox: the usual setup, lightbox: true with some images marked for panzoom.
C: panzoom match: auto: panzoom picks the images itself.
D: explicit marking: images marked with .panzoom or #| classes: panzoom.

And one page of its own:

E: formats and wide figures: 100 × 5 inch collages, and webp, svg and pdf output.

title: B: panzoom on marked images, Quarto’s lightbox on for the rest
text:
NoteAbout this page



This page tests the usual setup: Quarto’s lightbox is on for the document (lightbox: true), and only some images are marked for panzoom, with .panzoom or #| classes: panzoom. The markup is the same as in d-panzoom-selective, which has no lightbox.
The marked images should open the pan/zoom viewer; every other image should open Quarto’s lightbox, as in a-lightbox. Case 6’s first chunk has both classes: panzoom and #| lightbox: options on purpose: panzoom should win, so it doesn’t join GLightbox’s gallery. Case 8 (#| lightbox: false) gets neither. Case 9’s link should still work (images inside links are left alone).

title: D: panzoom filter, no document lightbox key (selective mode)
text:
NoteAbout this page



This page tests the panzoom extension. The panzoom filter is on, and the images marked with .panzoom or #| classes: panzoom should open the pan/zoom viewer. The document has no lightbox: key, so Quarto’s lightbox only applies where a case asks for it (the #| lightbox: cell options in cases 6 and 7). Case 6’s first chunk has both on purpose: panzoom should win, and its #| lightbox: options are dropped, so it doesn’t join GLightbox’s gallery. Case 9’s link should still work (images inside links are left alone).
Compare each case with the same numbered case in a-lightbox, which renders the same cases with Quarto’s lightbox alone.

6. R chunks with lightbox cell options (group + description)
This one also has classes: panzoom (conflict test).

```{r}
#| fig-cap: Simple demo R plot
#| classes: panzoom
#| lightbox:
#|   group: r-graph
#|   description: This is 1 to 10 plot

plot(1:10, rnorm(10))
```




Simple demo R plot




This one has only the lightbox options.

```{r}
#| fig-cap: Plot about cars data
#| lightbox:
#|   group: r-graph
#|   description: We see our cars data above

plot(cars)
```




Plot about cars data

7. Multi-plot cell, list-valued options

```{r}
#| classes: panzoom
#| fig-cap:
#|   - Caption for first plot
#|   - Caption for second plot
#| lightbox:
#|   group: cars
#|   description:
#|     - Description for first graph
#|     - Description for second graph

plot(mtcars)
plot(cars)
```
